text:
ara: Heads-up — noticed a sawtooth on our p99 for hosted-small on the tail windows after last week's kernel fallback change. p50 stable, p95 a little up, but p99 spikes every ~10m. anyone on this?
mike: I saw that too. looks correlated with bursts that force fallback to the slow kernel after KV miss storms.
sofia: can you paste the perf trace? curious if it's batching or kv eviction related.
ara: short traces attached below (snippet):
```
2026-03-10T14:12:03Z host=hs-12 trace_id=xyz latency_ms=18 kernel=fast kv_hit=true
2026-03-10T14:12:04Z host=hs-12 trace_id=abc latency_ms=220 kernel=fallback kv_hit=false
2026-03-10T14:12:05Z host=hs-12 trace_id=def latency_ms=19 kernel=fast kv_hit=true
```
jin: That pattern is classic: microburst causes queue to reach max_batch_tokens, triggers fallback, then tail. We tuned `max_wait_ms` earlier to 8ms which helps throughput but increases chance of fallback on transient KV cold.
sam: do we know which threshold causes kernel switch? is it batch token count or headroom?
mike: kernel picker currently prefers fast kernel when sequence length < 1024 and batch_tokens < 64; fallback if batch_tokens > 80 or kv_miss_ratio > 0.2. but the telemetry for kv_miss_ratio is noisy.
sofia: Could be that auto-batching coalesces too aggressively in short bursts. If `max_batch_tokens` is high, a single long request will inflate batch token count and trigger slow path. maybe try capping per-request tokens or reduce `max_wait_ms`.
ara: proposal: run short A/B for 6 hours: group A keep current (max_wait_ms=8, max_batch_tokens=256), group B reduce max_wait_ms=4 and max_batch_tokens=192. measure p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
jin: +1 but also enable a KV prefetch probe on group B for 10% traffic to see if kv cold misses are driving fallback. add a counter for kv_miss_ratio over 30s windows.
mike: added probe config: `--probe-kv-prefetch=0.1 --probe-window=30s` — pushed to staging.
ara: quick perf baseline from last 2h (hosted-small): tokens/s=18k, p95=40ms, p99=220ms, fallback_rate=0.8%
sofia: for the experiment we'll track: p50/p95/p99, fallback_rate, average batch_tokens, kv_miss_ratio, and end-to-end throughput.
sam: what about kernel selection hysteresis? if it flips too fast we get oscillation. can we add a short cooldown (200ms) after a fallback before allowing another fallback decision?
jin: we already have a 100ms cooloff, bumping to 250ms might smooth tail at cost of slightly more work on a degraded kernel. worth trying in B.
ara: agreed. update experiment group B: max_wait_ms=4, max_batch_tokens=192, kv_probe=10%, cooloff=250ms. roll will be gradual.
deploy-bot: deploy started: rollout group B to 12% of hosted-small at 2026-03-11T02:00:00Z — build=rlz-2026-03-11-12
mike: monitoring dashboards hooked. will alert if throughput drops >10% or p99 rises >20%.
sofia: small note — if p99 improves but throughput drops >5% we should examine unit-cost impact (tokens/second per GPU). don't trade SLO for too much cost.
ara: agreed. owners: mike + jin. experiment ends after 6h unless alerts. will report results here.
jin: initial 30m snapshot: group B p95=38ms (-5%), p99=160ms (-27%), tokens/s unchanged, kv_miss_ratio probe shows slight dip. promising.
sam: nice. keep an eye on kernel handoff count.
ara: thanks all — will post final numbers.
